title: U.N. Warns of ‘Another Wave of Atrocities’ in Sudan’s Civil War
content: Paramilitary groups have intensified an offensive on a crucial region bordering Darfur, prompting fears of another massacre.

title: After Years of Debate, Vatican Says No to Women Deacons, at Least for Now
content: But a papal commission examining the question said further study was required, and advised that women should be given other leadership roles in the Catholic Church.

title: Aid Workers Stand Trial for Helping to Smuggle People Into Greece
content: The activists provided support to people who sought sanctuary in Greece during Europe’s migration crisis.

title: Groups Express Anixety as Trump Threatens to Derail U.S.-Mexico-Canada Trade Pact
content: Hearings that began Wednesday in Washington reflected anxiety over the future of the U.S.-Mexico-Canada trade pact and whether the president could end up scrapping it.

title: Yasser Abu Shabab, Militant Leader Backed by Israel, Is Killed in Gaza, Official Says
content: Yasser Abu Shabab, a Bedouin man in his 30s, was at the center of an Israeli project in Gaza to build up anti-Hamas militias.

title: His Group Made World-Class Measurements of Atomic Elements
content: Yuri Ralchenko led one of the oldest teams at the National Institute for Standards and Technology. The fate of some experiments hangs in the air.

title: Amid Russian Sabotage, U.K. Points Finger at Putin Over Novichok Death
content: A British woman died from exposure to a nerve agent because of a botched assassination plot that the Russian leader must have authorized, an official report found.

title: Deadly Attacks in Gaza Test Cease-Fire as Body of Another Captive Is Returned
content: Israel launched a military strike after it said Hamas militants attacked its soldiers, the latest clashes in the two months since a truce was signed.

title: Cambodia Shuts Down Group That Laundered Billions in Scam Profits
content: A New York Times investigation in March found that Huione’s group of companies were at the heart of a global money laundering network for fraudsters, scammers and hackers.

title: Ruined Rice Fields and Broken Rail Lines: Sri Lanka Counts Cost of Cyclone
content: Officials estimate the damage runs into billions of dollars, a headache for the island nation just recovering from an economic crash.

title: How Israel’s Settlement Surge in the West Bank Is Displacing Palestinians
content: The Israeli government authorized 22 settlements in May, the largest expansion in decades, and Palestinian families are now being forced from their homes.

title: Spain Sees Itself as a Beacon for Immigrants. So Do Many Latin Americans.
content: The government presents its migrant policy as a welcoming alternative to U.S. crackdowns. But activists say those arriving on boats from Africa are excluded from that embrace.

title: Snail Theft Hits France Before Holiday Rush
content: Shop owners say the thieves who took 990 pounds of snails must have been escargot cognoscenti.

title: The Diplomat Who Was Accused of Sexual Abuse but Kept His Job
content: President William Ruto faces pressure after a Times investigation showed that his government downplayed or ignored the mistreatment of women working in Saudi Arabia.

title: Macron Urges Xi to Help End War in Ukraine
content: As President Emmanuel Macron of France visited China, its leader, Xi Jinping, said his country would play a constructive role in ending the fighting.
